previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old male with a history of AML in remission following stem cell transplant and chronic extensive sclerodermic skin GVHD was admitted for worsening foot pain and evaluation of a skin GVHD flare. He had no signs of active infection, with negative blood cultures and normal white count. Empiric Zosyn was started but discontinued after no growth was found. Dermatology recommended changes to his topical regimen including clobetasol, silver sulfadiazine, and collagenase ointment. MRI of the right ankle showed no tendonitis or tear, with findings attributed to nonspecific muscle edema and skin changes from GVHD. Liver enzymes were elevated, likely due to antibiotics, and expected to resolve. Pain was controlled with oral oxycodone, and the patient was discharged home after three days with updated wound care instructions and follow-up plans.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ yo M h/o AML s/p SCT and DLI, chronic GVHD with 
sclerodermatous changes who presented with SOB, malaise, and 
cough, found to have pneumonia.

#PNA: 
Infectious ddx included bacterial vs. viral vs. atypical. CT 
with bilateral lower lobe nodular ground-glass opacities 
concerning for pneumonia. Viral swab rapid antigen and culture 
negative. IgG level slightly low. Treated initially with 
vancomycin, cefepime, and 5 day course of azithromycin. 
Vancomycin discontinued after 7 days, and pt remained on 
cefepime for a 10 day course. Pt received q4 week IVIG dose on 
___. Initially required ___ supplemental O2. During admission, 
respiratory status improved, and oxygen was weaned. Although 
infectious studies did not identify pathogen, bronchoscopy was 
not pursued given clinical improvement. IL-2 (which pt is on as 
part of chronic GVHD trial) was initially held given infection, 
and was restarted during admission.

#Acute sinusitis: Following treatment of pneumonia, patient 
complained of persistent cough and nasal congestion. CT sinus 
and mandible suggested inflammatory changes. ENT was consulted 
and visualized pus in the sinuses. Samples were taken and sent 
for aerobic, anaerobic and fungal cultures. The patient was 
started on nasal irrigation treatment. Antibiotics were not 
started in discussion with ID as the patient had just finished a 
course of cefepime and was clinically stable.  

#Knee pain: 
Pt developed knee pain of unclear etiology. X rays showed 
calcifications throughout the lower leg.

# AML:
Continued on prophylaxis with acyclovir, atovaquone, 
posaconazole.

# Chronic GVHD: 
Pt did not have or develop signs of skin infection. Was given 
wound care with dakins, hydrophor, silver sulfadene, and 
dressings. Per above, IL2 therapy was initially held given 
infection; was restarted ___. Continued on prednisone 10mg 
daily and mycophenolate.

# Loose stools: 
Pt briefly had loose stools, which resolved. C diff negative.

#h/o HTN: 
Home amlodipine was held given pneumonia. 

# Hypothyroidism: 
Continued on levothyroxine.

#Depression:
Continued on paroxetine and given ativan prn anxiety.

4.  Minimally increased signal in the semimembranosus tendon suggest mild
degenerative change, but no abnormality at the tendon insertion.
5. No meniscal or ligament tear or osteoarthritis. 
6. Apparent limited range of motion, with the knee imaged in flexion.
